### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via stageField (symbol, a field of const object StrictObject))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via stageField (symbol, a field of const object StrictObject))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d40e07ddff9ffc617061cb3a4d74f62911f2dac2` — the merge of head `5645c2cd9f10036a302a2321ea42ad387129eb07` into base `8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d40e07ddff9ffc617061cb3a4d74f62911f2dac2 && git checkout d40e07ddff9ffc617061cb3a4d74f62911f2dac2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89 5645c2cd9f10036a302a2321ea42ad387129eb07 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89 && git merge --no-ff 5645c2cd9f10036a302a2321ea42ad387129eb07

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5645c2cd9f10036a302a2321ea42ad387129eb07`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.test.ts, .changeset/24198-blueprint-option-kind-stage-field.md, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json, content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx (the whole diff — no remainder is left at TIER_DEFAULT), read beside the cited code on `main` `8259ea03e2`: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`SelectOptionSchema.kind`, the kind-on-a-multi-value-field refusal), packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (`refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds`, `ObjectSchema.stageField`), packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES`), packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/scripts/solution-blueprint-header-row.test.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs; precedent PR #24152 (card #24129) by its file list and changeset.

Inputs: card #24198 (body; comments 6238179039 triage, 6238356000 dispatch claim, 6239509257 os-dev report), PR #24213 (body, file list, net diff against `main`, its one bot comment — the docs-drift advisory), and the check-runs on the head. Reads only: a `git fetch` of `main` and the branch, `git show` on both, and `record-recognisers --template --paths` for the hits (offline, no board). Nothing was built, run or re-run; the ablation and gate readings below are the dev's, named as such.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Lenient `BlueprintFieldSchema.options[].kind`** — `optionKindEnum().optional()`. Widens: a key the plain `z.object` stripped is now carried, and only `open` / `won` / `lost` is accepted (pinned at `objects.0.fields.1.options.2.kind`, `invalid_value`). RIGHT. The corner where a document that smuggled an off-vocabulary `kind` through the strip is now refused is not a narrowing of any declared contract: the key was undeclared, and the strict mirror — the only producer path — forbade it as an additional property.
2. **Lenient `BlueprintObjectSchema.stageField`** — `z.string().regex(SNAKE_CASE).optional()`, beside `nameField`, the string arm only. RIGHT: card scope item 2 names a snake_case field name; `ObjectSchema.stageField` is `z.union([z.string(), z.literal(false)])` and the `false` arm is deliberately not carried (③ item 8). Non-snake_case is refused at `objects.0.stageField`, `invalid_format` — pinned.
3. **Strict `StrictField.options[].kind`** — `optionKindEnum().nullable()`, present-required like every key in the mirror. Its JSON-Schema form is the nullable enum `StrictView.type` already uses, so the OpenAI-strict invariants (every key in `required`, `additionalProperties: false`) hold by the same construction. RIGHT. Pinned: null accepted, absence refused at exactly `objects.0.fields.1.options.1.kind`, off-vocabulary refused there too.
4. **Strict `StrictObject.stageField`** — `strictIdentOrNull(...)`, the helper `nameField` uses. RIGHT. Pinned: null accepted, absence refused at `objects.0.stageField`, non-snake refused.
5. **Enum reuse by identity, not by spelling** — `optionKindEnum` is an arrow function returning `SelectOptionSchema.shape.kind.unwrap()`. `SelectOptionSchema` is a `lazySchema` wrapping a `strictObject(...)` factory, `strictObject` returns the `ZodObject` type, so `.shape` is typed and the proxy resolves it; `kind` there is `z.enum([...]).optional().describe().meta()`, so `.unwrap()` is the inner enum instance, and each side's `.optional()` / `.nullable()` / `.describe()` clones a wrapper around it without touching the shared enum or its registry metadata. `field.zod.ts` is not edited and `SelectOption`'s accept set is unchanged. The identity test pins both sides `toBe` the same instance and the vocabulary `['open', 'won', 'lost']`. RIGHT. One comment inaccuracy, non-blocking: the docblock says the function form keeps a module-level read from forcing `SelectOptionSchema` at import, but `StrictField` is an eager module-level `z.object`, so `optionKindEnum()` runs at import of this module regardless. Harmless — one small schema, and I found no pin on import-time laziness — and the function form costs nothing.
6. **The describes** (public: they ship in both JSON Schemas and on the reference page), read against the code they cite. The per-option refusal at `['fields', f, 'options', i, 'kind']`, the picklist refusal and the multi-value refusal at `['stageField']` (gated on `hasOptionSource`), `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES = {select, radio}`, and the field schema's refusal of `kind` on any other field's options at `['options', i, 'kind']` — the four describes state these correctly, and "absent reads as open" is `SelectOption.kind`'s own sentence. ADR-0085 is the right citation (it types `stageField`). One over-statement, non-blocking: "refuses the object unless the field `stageField` names is a single-value `select` or `radio` whose inline options EACH declare `kind`" — the parse does not refuse a `stageField` naming a field with no options at all, or a non-select field without options (the docblock lists both as unchanged on purpose; lint `validate-semantic-roles` reports the dangling pointer). No accept set turns on that sentence, and the stricter reading steers the model to the one shape that passes both parse and lint. Recorded, not a defect.
7. **The contract leg** — a 1:1 copy of a parsed blueprint object into `ObjectSchema` parses, and dropping one option's `kind` is refused at exactly `['fields', 'status', 'options', 3, 'kind']` (`custom`). This pins that the blueprint spellings ARE the object schema's spellings, so `apply_blueprint` copies and converts nothing. RIGHT.
8. **Parity pins** — a new option-level key pin (both sides `['kind', 'label', 'value']`), the object pin now names `stageField` outright, and the strict fixtures gained `stageField: null` / `kind: null` so the leading-digit VALUE-parity pin fails for the digit alone. RIGHT.
9. **Generated artefacts, each against what the source change implies**: `authorable-surface/ai.json` gains `ai/BlueprintObject:stageField` only — the option `kind` sits in an anonymous inline object under the existing `ai/BlueprintField:options` row, as the precedent's `BlueprintView:filters` did; `authorable-surface.base.json` is the deletion-gate anchor (`--update-base`), untouched by an addition — right. `api-surface`: `optionKindEnum` and `STAGE_FIELD_RULE` are module-private, no export moves — unchanged, right. `json-schema.manifest`: no new def — unchanged, right. `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`: no `.refine()` added (`.regex` projects as `pattern`, the enum projects) — unchanged, right; the precedent moved it only for its `filters.element` refinement. The strictness-ledger `ai/` shard: `z.object(` sites 26 on `main`, 26 at the head — unchanged, right. `content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx`: regenerated, carries both keys in all four tables plus the new nested `BlueprintField.options[number]` table. The published `json-schema/ai/SolutionBlueprintStrict.json` is gitignored; its strict invariants are pinned at parse level (`requires both keys to be present`) and by construction (item 3).
10. **Header-row pin** (`scripts/solution-blueprint-header-row.test.ts`): the module doc block and the blank line separating it from `const SNAKE_CASE` are unchanged — the only header-zone change is the import on line 5 — and the corpus row in `skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md` is unchanged. RIGHT.
11. **Boundaries**: `field.zod.ts` and `object.zod.ts` read, not edited; no cloud or objectui path; no governed path in the file list; draft PR, assignee `os-project-manager`; the dispatch `Claim:` names this branch and the dev posted no second claim.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/24198-blueprint-option-kind-stage-field.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `minor`, `Clause-②: yes` on its own line; the PR body carries the same line, key-initial, as its third line. Both read as a widening: `clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes` and `yes (widening)` as one declaration (an absent arm declares no direction; `yes` already means widening), so the dev's flagged mismatch with the card's `yes (widening)` is spelling, not substance.
- What publishes: two lenient keys (the accept set grows) and two strict keys. The strict mirror formally loses documents lacking the two keys, but it is the `generateObject` output contract, regenerated per call and never persisted (module header), whose only producer generates against the schema it is handed; the changeset's last bullet says so ("a producer of the STRICT shape must now send `stageField` on each object and `kind` on each option"), exactly as precedent PR #24152's changeset did for `filters` / `sort`, which landed `minor` under `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. No `(narrowing)` arm is owed; nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 marker.
- `minor` matches the diff. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. Each `deviations` entry and the one `out_of_scope_findings` entry of report 6239509257, answered:

1. `Clause-②: yes` vs the card's `yes (widening)` — equivalent readings (② above); no action.
2. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally — it is hosted by ci.yml's `Build Core`, green on the head; answered by the gate.
3. `test:repo` not run locally — the header-row test's two inputs are unchanged (① item 10); Test Core carries it, state recorded below.
4. A concurrent turbo build rebuilt `packages/spec/dist` mid-gate and the 13 overlapped gates were re-run — a note about the dev's local readings; the gate verdicts of record are the head's check-runs; nothing to escalate.
5. The first ablation leg was a no-op (bad log path) and was re-run — the cited run is the second; the ablation is the dev's measurement and was not re-run here (read-only). The predicted direction is consistent with the pins I read: renaming either key fails the key-parity pins by construction.
6. `origin/main` moved six commits after the pre-PR merge and no second merge was made — the net diff here is computed against current `main` `8259ea03e2` and applies cleanly; `mergeable_state: blocked` is the draft flag plus unfinished required checks, not a conflict; §10 asks for a merge only on a conflict, a main-caused red or a queue removal. Right.
7. Four pushes — the push-each-step rule; no flag.
8. `stageField: false` has no blueprint spelling (noted, not filed) — accepted as noted. The card scopes a snake_case field name; a blueprint that omits `stageField` keeps the platform's heuristic detection, which is the behaviour before this PR; the named consumer (objectstack-ai/cloud#2926) asks for the kinds, not for "declared non-linear" from the design step. Not a defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap under Prime Directive 10, so no issue is owed; a producer wanting the `false` arm from the blueprint is a new card.
9. The seat's `stageField` premise (it rides the card iff `ObjectSchema.stageField` is the only trigger of the mandatory-kind rule) — confirmed on `main` `8259ea03e2`: one definition (`object.zod.ts:1970`), one call (`:3160`, with `object.stageField`), and no other `stageField` declaration in `packages/spec/src` besides `object.zod.ts:2897`. The fork the seat reserved did not open.
10. Reviewer notes, both non-blocking, carried in ① items 5 and 6: the `optionKindEnum` function rationale is moot (the strict side is eager), and `STAGE_FIELD_RULE` over-states the parse refusal for an options-less target field. Neither moves an accept set; neither is a FAIL condition.
11. Docs-drift advisory on the PR: three hand-written pages and one release page name `stageField` — the object's key, not the blueprint's; nothing in this diff touches them; advisory only.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-17T19:39Z: 39 check-runs; 27 success (the gate-carrying names among them: Build Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Spec property liveness, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates); 5 skipped (full-battery lanes not run on a PR: Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate (the per-shard matrix row, named with a template placeholder), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)); 7 in_progress: Test Core (1/6), Test Core (2/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (4/6), Test Core (5/6), Test Core (6/6), Type Check · workspace. The gate verdicts are the check-runs' own; the contract verdict below is mine. The unfinished lanes are recorded as unfinished: this record does not call them green, and the queue guard reads them at landing.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · PR #24213 @ `5645c2cd9f` (#24198) · `domain:spec` seat 1 · `os-project-manager` · session `session_01TyRhWbVbbQpQJTDbW8VahJ` · 2026-10-17T20:00Z

Reviewer of record. Every item below was checked against GitHub and the code, not against the report (`6239509257` on #24198).

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`. The first line is `Fixes #24198`, the body's only closing keyword, then `Clause-②: yes`, matching claim `6238356000`. 5 files, +241/−7, assignee `os-project-manager`. Not governed: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 24213` reads 0 of 5 paths on the register, under 3000 lines.
- **Premise, measured by the seat before dispatch** (`f963d8e2b`): neither blueprint shape had `kind` on its options or `stageField` on its objects; `SelectOption.kind` sits at `field.zod.ts:452`; `refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds` is called once, with `object.stageField` (`object.zod.ts:3160`).
- **The seat's scope call holds:** `stageField` rides this card on the measured premise that `ObjectSchema.stageField` is the rule's only trigger. The dev and the contract review both confirmed that premise on `main`.
- **What it lands:**
  - Lenient: `options[].kind` (optional, `SelectOption.kind`'s enum by identity) and `stageField` (optional snake_case).
  - Strict mirror: both keys present-required and nullable, in the same form as `StrictView.type` and the #24152 precedent.
  - Parity and contract-leg pins; the `authorable-surface` row and the reference page regenerated; a `minor` changeset.
  - The changeset's sentences were read against the diff. "A producer of the STRICT shape must now send `stageField` on each object and `kind` on each option (null when it has none)" is the honest producer consequence of the strict pattern. "The object schema's `false` value has no blueprint spelling" matches the diff.
- **Contract review:** PASS `6239776296` on this head (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`). It agrees with `minor` and `Clause-②: yes`. Its two non-blocking notes stand as notes: the `optionKindEnum` laziness comment is moot, and the `stageField` describe over-states the parse refusal for an options-less field (lint reports that case).

- **Deviations, accepted:**
  - `Clause-②: yes` carried verbatim from the claim;
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` declared to CI;
  - `test:repo` declared to CI;
  - an overlapping local build, with the 13 affected gates re-run green;
  - one ablation leg first ran as a no-op and was re-run;
  - no second `main` merge: no overlap.
- **Out-of-scope finding:** the blueprint has no spelling for `stageField: false`: dropped — no producer or consumer of that form is named, and the PR's Acceptance notes record it.

The PR goes to the merge queue in this act. objectstack-ai/cloud#2926 can start once cloud's pin carries this merge.
